blocks.content: The service conditions of constitutional authorities cannot be varied to their disadvantage after their appointment.

rows: Explicitly provisioned under the Constitution of India
Created by an Act of Parliament or State Legislature
Fixed by Parliament; cannot be varied to disadvantage post-appointment
Determined by executive rules or statutory regulations
High; removal only via constitutional impeachment/address procedure
Subject to statutory provisions or pleasure of executive
Strictly barred from further government appointments in most cases
Subject to specific statutory provisions of the parent Act

items: Differentiate between expenditure 'charged upon' vs 'made from' the Consolidated Fund of India regarding parliamentary voting rights.
Remember that removal of constitutional post-holders requires a special majority in both Houses of Parliament on grounds of proved misbehaviour or incapacity.
Note that service conditions of civil servants under Article 309 can be regulated by executive rules until Parliament enacts a specific law.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Appointments to key constitutional offices are made directly by the President of India by warrant under his hand and seal.
Service conditions and tenure are governed by Acts of Parliament to secure independence from executive pressure.
Salaries and allowances of constitutional heads are charged upon the Consolidated Fund of India and are non-votable.
Post-tenure disability bars incumbents from further employment under the Government of India or any State government.
